source_text:
tu muta istum contradictorem, qui una hora in cruce mutasti latronem.\'
Et certe uideamus quid habes. \'habeo,\' inquis, \'sacramentum, habeo baptismum*. si dicam tibi \'proba\', ostendis mihi quid acceperis, dicis quid confessus fueris, dicis quid teneas. agnosco, non muto, non exsufflo; absit ut, cum quaero salutem desertoris, faciam iniuriam imperatori. ergo probasti mihi quod habeas sacramentum; exponendo sacramentum probasti mihi te habere fidem. proba mihi quod habeas caritatem: tene unitatem. nolo mihi dicas \'habeo caritatem\': proba. unum patrem habemus: simul oremus. quid tu dicis, quando oras, rogo te? \'pater noster qui es in caelis.\' deo gratias. secundum magisterium domini nostri addidisti: qui es in caelis. singulos enim patres habebamus in terris, unum inuenimus simul in caelis. pater noster qui es in caelis: ipsum inuocas patrem. pater noster unam coniugem habere uoluit. qui ergo adoramus unum patrem, quare non agnoscimus unam matrem? si natum te dicis de alia, et de sinu alieno ipsa te peperit. quod dixi, non omnes intellegere potuistis. nouimus per legitimas coniuges factum esse, ut etiam, qui non de legitimis coniugibus nascerentur, in eadem hereditate sociarentur. hoc uoluntas coniugis fecit. nam Ismahel exheredatus est. ipsum Sara pepererat, etsi de utero alieno. Sara pepererat utero alieno, uoto suo. ipsa enim dixit: uolo enim de ista mihi filios facias, et ideo fecit Abraham. uxor enim non habet potestatem corporis sui, sed uir; similiter uir non habet potestatem corporis sui, sed mulier. nam filius esset, si non superbisset; superbus est exheredatus Ismahel. erexit enim ancilla ceruicem, ut diceretur: eice ancillam et filium eius; non enim heres erit filius ancillae cum filio meo Isaac. nam uis nosse quid ualeat pax, quid ualeat concordia, quid ualeat humilitas, et quid impediat superbia? Ismahelem exheredauit, filios autem ancillarum de Iacob, quia et illi ut nascerentur coniugia iusta uoluerunt, filios ergo ancillarum de Iacob nouimus in unam hereditatem aduocatos. simul numerati sunt omnes patriarchae duodecim; nullum ab altero uteri diuersitas separauit, quia omnes caritas sociauit. quid interest ergo ubi baptismum acceperis? baptismus meus est, dicit tibi Sara, baptismus meus est, dicit tibi Rachel. noli superbire, ueni ad hereditatem, maxime quia ipsa hereditas non est illa terra quae data est filiis Iacob. filiis Israel data est terra; quanto a pluribus possidebatur, tanto plus angustabatur. hereditas nostra pax uocatur; testamentum lego: pacem meam do uobis, pacem meam relinquo uobis. simul teneamus quod diuidi non potest. non eam angustat numerosus possessor, quanticumque uenerint, sicut promissum est: sic erit semen tuum tamquam stellae caeli et sicut arena quae est ad labium maris. in semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes. et uidi, inquit in Apocalypsi, multos in stolis albis et habentes palmas, quos numerare nemo potest, uenientes ex omnibus gentibus. ueniant, pacem teneant. angusta non fit nostra possessio; angustias non facit nisi sola dissensio. ecce, fratres mei, ut angustias adhuc patiamur, dissensio facit fratris nostri: consentiat in pace, et facta est latitudo.
orientation: Augustine is addressing Emeritus directly, testing what he claims to possess and urging him to prove his love by entering Catholic unity.
pass_a_gloss: you [sg.] change that contradictor, [you] who in one hour on [the] cross changed [the] thief. And certainly let us see what you have. 'I have,' you say, 'the sacrament, I have baptism. If I say to you 'prove [it]', you show me what you have received, you say what you have confessed, you say what you hold. I acknowledge, I do not change, I do not exsufflate; far be it that, when I seek [the] salvation of [a] deserter, I do injury to [the] emperor. Therefore you have proved to me that you have [the] sacrament; by expounding [the] sacrament you have proved to me [that] you have faith. Prove to me that you have charity: hold unity. I do not want [that] you say to me 'I have charity': prove [it]. One father we have: together let us pray. What do you say, when you pray, I ask you? 'Our father who art in [the] heavens.' Thanks to God. According to [the] teaching of our Lord you have added: who art in [the] heavens. For single fathers we were having on earth, one we have found together in [the] heavens. Our father who art in [the] heavens: him you invoke [as] father. Our father one wife to have willed. Therefore [we] who adore one father, why do we not acknowledge one mother? If born you say [yourself] from another, and from [the] bosom of another she herself bore you. What I have said, not all have been able to understand. We know through lawful wives [it] to have been done, that also, [those] who not from lawful wives were born, in the same inheritance were joined. This [the] will of [the] wife did. For Ishmael [was] disinherited. Him Sarah had borne, even if from [the] womb of another. Sarah had borne [him] from [the] womb of another, by her vow. For she herself said: I wish for from her to me sons you make, and therefore Abraham did [it]. For [the] wife does not have power of her own body, but [the] husband; similarly [the] husband does not have power of his own body, but [the] woman. For [a] son he would be, if he had not been proud; proud [was] disinherited Ishmael. For [the] maidservant raised [her] neck, so that it was said: cast out [the] maidservant and her son; for not [an] heir will be [the] son of [the] maidservant with my son Isaac. For do you wish to know what peace avails, what concord avails, what humility avails, and what pride impedes? Ishmael it disinherited, but [the] sons of [the] maidservants from Jacob, because they also that they might be born lawful marriages willed, [the] sons therefore of [the] maidservants from Jacob we know into one inheritance [were] called. Together [were] numbered all [the] patriarchs twelve; none from another [the] diversity of [the] womb separated, because all charity joined. What does it matter therefore where you have received baptism? My baptism is, says to you Sarah, my baptism is, says to you Rachel. Do not be proud, come to [the] inheritance, especially because that inheritance is not that land which was given to [the] sons of Jacob. To [the] sons of Israel was given [the] land; by how many more it was possessed, by so much more it was crowded. Our inheritance peace is called; [the] testament I read: my peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you. Together let us hold what cannot be divided. Not it crowds [the] numerous possessor, however many have come, as [it] has been promised: so will be your seed as [the] stars of [the] heaven and as [the] sand which is at [the] lip of [the] sea. In your seed will be blessed all [the] nations. And I saw, he says in [the] Apocalypse, many in white robes and having palms, whom to number no one is able, coming from all [the] nations. Let them come, let them hold peace. Not narrow becomes our possession; narrowness does not make except only dissension. Behold, my brothers, that narrowness still we suffer, dissension makes [it] of our brother: let him agree in peace, and [it] has become breadth.

choices.why: Keeps the literal physical action of exsufflation, which Augustine denies doing to the sacrament.
Matches the glossary term for one who has left the Catholic Church.
Uses the glossary rendering for caritas, the love without which sacraments profit nothing.
Uses the glossary rendering for the unity of the Catholic Church.
Uses the glossary rendering for the shared inheritance of peace and promise.
Uses the glossary rendering for the peace Christ gives, identified with unity.

pass_b_english: You changed the thief on the cross in one hour: change this opposer too. And surely let us see what you have. "I have," you say, "the sacrament, I have baptism." If I say to you, "Prove it," you show me what you received, you say what you confessed, you say what you hold. I recognize it, I do not change it, I do not breathe scorn upon it. Far be it from me that, when I seek the salvation of a deserter, I should insult the emperor. So you have proved to me that you have the sacrament; by explaining the sacrament you have proved to me that you have the faith. Prove to me that you have love: hold unity. I do not want you to say to me, "I have love." Prove it. We have one Father: let us pray together. What do you say when you pray, I ask you? "Our Father, who art in heaven." Thanks be to God. According to the teaching of our Lord you added: who art in heaven. For we each had fathers on earth; we have found one Father together in heaven. Our Father, who art in heaven: you call upon Him as Father. Our Father willed to have one wife. Why then, when we worship one Father, do we not recognize one mother? If you say you were born of another, she herself bore you from a foreign bosom. What I said, not all of you could understand. We know that through lawful wives it came about that even those who were not born of lawful wives were joined in the same inheritance. The will of the spouse did this. For Ishmael was disinherited. Sarah herself had borne him, though from another's womb. Sarah bore him from another's womb, by her own wish. For she said: I want you to make me children by her (Genesis 16:2), and so Abraham did it. For the wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does (1 Corinthians 7:4). For he would have been a son, if he had not been proud; Ishmael was disinherited for pride. For the maidservant raised her neck, so that it was said: Cast out the maidservant and her son; for the son of the maidservant shall not be heir with my son Isaac (Genesis 21:10). Do you want to know what peace is worth, what concord is worth, what humility is worth, and what pride blocks? Pride disinherited Ishmael, but the sons of the maidservants from Jacob—because the lawful wives also wished them to be born—the sons of the maidservants of Jacob, we know, were called into one inheritance. All twelve patriarchs were counted together; no difference of womb separated one from another, because love joined them all. What difference does it make then where you received baptism? "Baptism is mine," Sarah says to you; "baptism is mine," Rachel says to you. Do not be proud; come to the inheritance, especially because that inheritance is not the land that was given to the sons of Jacob. The land was given to the sons of Israel; the more people possessed it, the more crowded it became. Our inheritance is called peace. I read the testament: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave with you (John 14:27). Let us hold together what cannot be divided. Many possessors do not crowd it; however many come, as it was promised: So shall your offspring be, like the stars of heaven and like the sand that is on the shore of the sea (Genesis 22:17). In your offspring shall all nations be blessed (Genesis 22:18). And I saw, he says in Revelation, many in white robes and holding palm branches, whom no one could number, coming from all nations (Revelation 7:9). Let them come, let them hold peace. Our possession does not become narrow; only dissension makes narrowness. See, my brothers, so that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension is the cause: let him agree in peace, and breadth is made.

problems.quote: And surely let us see what you have.
problems.source_quote: tu muta istum contradictorem, qui una hora in cruce mutasti latronem.
problems.why: Source opens with prayer asking God to change Emeritus, citing the robber changed on the cross; English omits this entirely.
problems.fix: You changed that robber in one hour on the cross: change this opposer. And surely let us see what you have.
problems.ruling: Source opens 'tu muta istum contradictorem...latronem' (change this opponent...thief); English omits entire opening prayer, losing key rhetorical appeal and biblical parallel.

problems.quote: And surely let us see what you have
problems.why: Missing opening prayer to Christ; 'tu muta istum contradictorem' is Augustine's direct address to Jesus, not to Emeritus.
problems.fix: You changed the thief on the cross in a single hour: change this contradictor too. And surely let us see what you have.
problems.ruling: 'tu muta istum contradictorem... in cruce mutasti latronem' is a prayer to Christ; omitting it loses meaning and misleads the reader.

problems.quote: because lawful wives also willed that they be born
problems.source_quote: quia et illi ut nascerentur coniugia iusta uoluerunt
problems.why: Subject is the maidservants' sons, not lawful wives; 'coniugia iusta' are lawful marriages, not wives willing.
problems.fix: because lawful marriages too were willing for them to be born
problems.ruling: 'illi' refers to the sons; 'coniugia iusta uoluerunt' means they wanted lawful marriages, not 'lawful wives willed they be born.'

edits.old: And surely let us see what you have.
edits.new: You changed the thief on the cross in one hour: change this opposer too. And surely let us see what you have.

edits.old: because lawful wives also willed that they be born
edits.new: because lawful marriages also willed that they be born

fixed: Added the opening prayer to Christ, which the English omitted entirely.
Corrected the subject of 'uoluerunt' from lawful wives to lawful marriages, matching the source 'coniugia iusta'.

problems.quote: The will of the wife did this
problems.why: "Coniugis" is spouse/husband, not wife specifically; Sarah's will as Abraham's spouse, not generic wife.
problems.fix: The will of the spouse did this

problems.quote: that we still suffer narrowness is caused by the dissension of our brother
problems.source_quote: ut angustias adhuc patiamur, dissensio facit fratris nostri
problems.why: Awkward and misleading: "ut" expresses purpose/result (so that), not "that...is caused by".
problems.fix: so that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension makes it

problems.why: "Palmas" in context of white robes and Revelation 7:9 means palm branches, not palms of hands.
problems.ruling: habentes palmas in Revelation 7:9 context means holding palm branches, not palms of hands; misleads reader.

edits.old: The will of the wife did this.
edits.new: The will of the spouse did this.

edits.old: that we still suffer narrowness is caused by the dissension of our brother
edits.new: so that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension makes it

fixed: Changed 'wife' to 'spouse' for 'coniugis', which is masculine/feminine and refers to Sarah as Abraham's spouse.
Reworked the final clause to reflect the purpose/result sense of 'ut' and the active verb 'facit'.
Changed 'palms' to 'palm branches' for 'palmas' in the Revelation quotation.

problems.quote: I do not blow it out
problems.why: "Exsufflo" means to blow upon in contempt/exorcism, not extinguish; "blow out" suggests snuffing a candle.
problems.fix: I do not breathe scorn upon it, or I do not reject it with contempt.

problems.quote: she bore you from a foreign womb
problems.source_quote: et de sinu alieno ipsa te peperit
problems.why: Augustine says the mother (Church) bore you from a foreign bosom, not 'she bore you from a foreign womb.'
problems.fix: she herself bore you from a foreign bosom
problems.ruling: 'sinu' means bosom/lap, not womb; 'alieno' refers to another's bosom

problems.quote: It disinherited Ishmael, but the sons of the maidservants of Jacob
problems.source_quote: Ismahelem exheredauit, filios autem ancillarum de Iacob
problems.why: Subject of 'exheredauit' is pride (superbia), not 'it' vaguely; 'de Iacob' means 'from Jacob,' not 'of Jacob.'
problems.fix: Pride disinherited Ishmael, but the sons of the maidservants from Jacob
problems.ruling: 'de Iacob' means 'from Jacob,' not 'of Jacob'; 'it' obscures pride as subject

problems.quote: dissension makes it: let him agree in peace, and breadth is made
problems.source_quote: dissensio facit fratris nostri: consentiat in pace, et facta est latitudo
problems.why: Source says 'dissension makes our brother [narrow]'; English 'makes it' loses the brother reference.
problems.fix: dissension makes our brother: let him agree in peace, and breadth is made
problems.ruling: 'fratris nostri' is genitive: 'our brother's dissension,' not 'dissension makes our brother'

problems.quote: A numerous possessor does not crowd it
problems.why: "Numerosus possessor" means many possessors (plural implied by numerosus), not a single numerous one; collective sense lost.
problems.fix: Many possessors do not crowd it, or a great number of holders does not narrow it.
problems.ruling: Numerosus possessor is plural collective: 'many possessors.' 'A numerous possessor' misleads reader into singular.

problems.quote: See, my brothers, so that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension makes it
problems.source_quote: ecce, fratres mei, ut angustias adhuc patiamur, dissensio facit fratris nostri
problems.why: "Ut" here means "that" introducing result/complaint, not purpose "so that"; Augustine laments present suffering, not aims at it.
problems.fix: See, my brothers: that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension causes it.
problems.ruling: Ut angustias patiamur is result clause: 'that we suffer narrowness.' 'So that' implies purpose, distorts meaning.

edits.old: I do not blow it out.
edits.new: I do not breathe scorn upon it.

edits.old: she bore you from a foreign womb.
edits.new: she herself bore you from a foreign bosom.

edits.old: It disinherited Ishmael, but the sons of the maidservants of Jacob
edits.new: Pride disinherited Ishmael, but the sons of the maidservants from Jacob

edits.old: dissension makes it: let him agree in peace, and breadth is made.
edits.new: dissension makes our brother: let him agree in peace, and breadth is made.

edits.old: A numerous possessor does not crowd it
edits.new: Many possessors do not crowd it

edits.old: See, my brothers, so that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension makes it
edits.new: See, my brothers: that we still suffer narrowness, our brother's dissension causes it

fixed: exsufflo means to blow upon in contempt, not extinguish; changed to 'breathe scorn upon it'.
source has 'de sinu alieno ipsa te peperit' — 'ipsa' (she herself) and 'sinu' (bosom) were lost; restored.
source subject of 'exheredauit' is 'superbia' (pride), and 'de Iacob' means 'from Jacob'; corrected.
source 'dissensio facit fratris nostri' — the brother is the object of the narrowness; restored.
source 'numerosus possessor' is collective, meaning many possessors; corrected.
source 'ut angustias adhuc patiamur' is a result clause, not purpose; changed 'so that' to 'that' and 'makes' to 'causes'.

fixed.quote: because lawful marriages also willed that they be born
fixed.fix: because the lawful wives also wished them to be born
fixed.note: Here 'coniugia iusta' means Jacob's lawful wives, who wanted these sons born; 'marriages willed' hides who acted, and the checker's fix changes the meaning.

fixed.quote: our brother's dissension makes our brother
fixed.fix: our brother's dissension is the cause
fixed.note: The Latin says our brother's dissension causes the narrowness; 'makes our brother' is nonsense (the 'so that' just before the quote would also read better as 'that').

dismissed.quote: she herself bore you from a foreign bosom.
dismissed.why: 'ipsa' means 'she herself' bore YOU; English drops the pronoun 'te' (you), losing the direct address to Emeritus.
dismissed.note: The English already has 'bore you'; nothing is missing.
